_meta.purpose: Maps brand_key (used in tracked_concepts.target_key when target_type='brand') to public-company tickers. Loaded into the brand_to_ticker table at startup. The concept-extraction LLM proposes new brand keys; this file is the hand-curated authoritative answer for known brands so the LLM doesn't hallucinate the parent company.
_meta.philosophy: Bias toward consumer-facing brands the Social Arbitrage Engine will actually surface, weighted toward the 5 v1 source-type verticals (audio, sneakers, beauty, watches, photo, pcbuild) plus broader consumer/tech adjacencies. Skip megacap-obvious mappings (e.g. iPhone -> AAPL) that the LLM would never get wrong.
growth_path: Phase 0 (this file): 238 rows. Operator audits each. Catches the most common Social Arbitrage names across HN/4chan-driven concepts and 5 v1 verticals + AI/dev/cloud/crypto/EV/gaming adjacencies.

Phase 1: LLM concept extractor proposes new brand_keys when it sees an unrecognized brand. Operator reviews via /api/market-intelligence/brands/proposed endpoint. Approved ones land here with source_method='llm_assist' and confidence=0.6.
Phase 2-3: Backtest replay calibrates which brand mappings actually predicted moves. Misses get pruned. Gaps (brands the system saw move but didn't have mapped) get added.
Phase 5: Target ≥200 rows by end of Phase 5 per PRD §Phase 0 deliverables.
review_checklist_for_user: Verticals beyond v1 (ai_models, devtools, cloud_infra, semiconductors, crypto_brokers, ev_auto, gaming_media, restaurants, lifestyle_home, fintech_consumer, ai_hardware) — are these the right buckets for Phase 6 priority?

Many AI/devtools brands are PRIVATE (parent_ticker=null) — should we map them to the closest publicly-traded competitor as parent_ticker instead of leaving null? Current decision: keep null for cleanliness, use secondary_tickers for comp signal.
Some Asian listings (.KS, .TW, .T, .SW, .MI) — confirm scanner / portfolio system can route to those. If not, downgrade confidence to <0.5 to avoid auto-promotion.
Cross-listed brands (e.g. nike + jordan_brand + air_force_one + converse all under NKE): is this granularity right, or should we collapse?
Brand-key conflicts: nvidia_rtx (specific GPU franchise, original) vs nvidia (parent, new). Keep both? Promoter currently uses target_key directly.

schema.brand_key: snake_case stable id; UNIQUE; matches tracked_concepts.target_key when target_type='brand'
schema.parent_ticker: Primary public expression (the company that owns the brand or whose stock moves on brand momentum)
schema.secondary_tickers: Suppliers, retailers, or competitors that also benefit from the brand momentum signal
schema.confidence: 1.0 = hand_curated certain mapping; 0.6 = LLM-proposed pending review; lower = ambiguous
schema.vertical: Tagged for portfolio analysis; not stored in DB
schema.notes: Free-form audit notes; not stored in DB
